hints: Inserting or deleting at position 0 usually needs special code. Is there a trick that makes position 0 look like every other position?
A singly linked list with a dummy (sentinel) head and a size counter. For any index, walk index steps from the dummy to reach the node just before the target, then relink.

1. Keep a dummy node and size.
  2. get(i): if i is out of range return −1; else walk i+1 steps from dummy and return the value.
  3. addAtIndex(i, v): if i > size do nothing; walk i steps to prev; insert a new node after it; size++.
  4. addAtHead = addAtIndex(0, v); addAtTail = addAtIndex(size, v).
  5. deleteAtIndex(i): if valid, walk i steps to prev and set prev.next = prev.next.next; size−−.

approaches.name: ArrayList-backed
approaches.idea: Use a dynamic array; inserts and deletes shift elements (but it misses the point of practising nodes).

approaches.name: Optimal: singly linked list with sentinel
approaches.idea: Walk to the node before the index and relink. A tail pointer could make addAtTail O(1), but O(index) is fine here.

explain: Sample: addAtHead(5) → [5], addAtTail(9) → [5,9], addAtIndex(1,7) → [5,7,9], get(1) = 7, deleteAtIndex(0) → [7,9], get(0) = 7, get(4) = −1. Because every operation starts from the dummy, index 0 needs no special case. The size counter lets you reject invalid indexes before walking. Note addAtIndex with index equal to size is allowed (it appends).
recognize: 'Implement a list with get/add/delete at an index' → nodes plus a sentinel head and a size counter.
